# Configuration Reference

`.sdbx.yaml` is operator-owned project intent. The table below is generated from the same typed setting metadata used by the CLI, broker, and management UI.

Use `sdbx config get` to inspect values and `sdbx config set KEY VALUE` for one supported mutation. Each successful typed mutation validates the complete configuration, updates the lock, and regenerates managed runtime files.

## Core

| Key | Type | Default | Options | Typed mutation | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `domain` | `text` | `sdbx.example.com` | — | yes | Base DNS domain used to derive routed service URLs. |
| `expose.mode` | `select` | `lan` | lan, direct, cloudflared | yes | Ingress boundary: trusted LAN, direct public HTTPS, or a remote-managed Cloudflare Tunnel. |
| `expose.tunnel_protocol` | `select` | `http2` | http2, quic, auto | yes | Cloudflare exposure only: http2 uses TCP for reliable HTTP delivery; quic uses UDP; auto prefers QUIC with connection-failure fallback. |
| `expose.tls.email` | `text` | `""` | — | yes | Plain contact address required before direct-mode ACME certificates can be issued. |
| `timezone` | `text` | `Europe/Paris` | — | yes | IANA timezone propagated to supported containers. |

## Generated default shape

This is the current serialized shape before the setup wizard replaces placeholder choices. It is schema input, not a deployable unattended configuration.

```yaml
domain: sdbx.example.com
timezone: Europe/Paris
expose:
    mode: lan
    tls: {}
    tunnel_protocol: http2
routing:
    strategy: subdomain
    base_domain: sdbx
auth:
    factor: one_factor
config_path: ./configs
data_path: ./data
downloads_path: ./data/downloads
media_path: ./data/media
secrets_path: ./secrets
plex_enabled: false
jellyfin_enabled: false
puid: 1000
pgid: 1000
umask: "002"
vpn_enabled: false
torrent_peer_port: 6881
addons: []
```

## Direct HTTPS

Direct exposure supports ACME only in v1. The TLS provider is derived as `acme`; `expose.tls.email` must contain one plain contact address. Custom certificate-file fields are rejected because no supported generator path consumes them.

When changing an existing LAN or tunnel project, set the contact first, then change the exposure mode:

```bash
sdbx config set expose.tls.email ops@example.test
sdbx config set expose.mode direct
sdbx lock verify
```

## Service route overrides

`services` is a reviewed manual-intent map rather than a generic typed setting. An entry may override `routing`, `subdomain`, or `path` for one catalog service:

```yaml
services:
  sonarr:
    routing: path
    path: /television
```

This map cannot override an image, environment variable, volume, permission, network, or container policy. External source priority selects a complete `kind: Service` definition under the source trust rules; partial `kind: ServiceOverride` catalog documents are rejected.

After a manual edit, run `sdbx lock diff`, review the graph and route change, then run `sdbx lock` and `sdbx lock verify`. Use `sdbx generate` only when intent and the existing lock still agree.

## Path and credential rules

Relative managed paths must stay inside the project; absolute paths may not be filesystem roots. Move several path roots in one reviewed YAML edit so intermediate typed mutations do not create directories at an old/new mixture.

VPN usernames, passwords, private keys, tunnel tokens, claim tokens, service API keys, and backup credentials do not belong in project intent. A legacy `vpn_username` key is rejected with a migration instruction; provider credentials belong in `configs/gluetun/gluetun.env`.
